title: U.S. Senate · Tennessee

context.text: This election fills the Class II U.S. Senate seat held by Bill Hagerty (R), who first took office in January 2021. Hagerty advanced unopposed from the August 6, 2026 Republican primary. Marquita Bradshaw won the Democratic primary with 54.7% of the vote, defeating Maria Brewer, Kevin Lee McCants, Civil Miller-Watkins, and Diana Onyejiaka.
As of late September 2026, independent election forecasters (Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, Sabato's Crystal Ball, Decision Desk HQ) all rated the general election Solid/Safe Republican.

candidates.name: Bill Hagerty
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed from the August 6, 2026 Republican primary

summary.text: Bill Hagerty is the Republican U.S. Senator from Tennessee, seeking a second term. A Vanderbilt-trained lawyer, he worked in consulting and private equity, served in the George H.W. Bush administration, and was Tennessee's commissioner of economic and community development (2011-2014) and U.S. Ambassador to Japan (2017-2019). He was first elected to the Senate in 2020.

background.text: Born in Gallatin, Tennessee, and originally from Sumner County; he graduated from Madisonville North Hopkins High School in Kentucky and became an Eagle Scout.
Earned a bachelor's degree (1981) and a law degree (1984), both from Vanderbilt University.

Began his business career at Boston Consulting Group, including three years based in Tokyo, then worked in venture capital and private equity as an investor, executive and board member. According to Ballotpedia, he founded and was managing director of Hagerty Peterson & Company.
Worked in the George H. W. Bush administration on the domestic policy staff and as a White House Fellow, and served as national finance chair of Mitt Romney's 2008 presidential campaign.

From 2011 to 2014 he was Tennessee commissioner of economic and community development in Gov. Bill Haslam's cabinet; his official biography says he reorganized the department and cut over 40% of its positions.
Served on Donald Trump's 2016-2017 presidential transition team, where he oversaw presidential appointments.
Nominated by President Trump as U.S. Ambassador to Japan in March 2017, he was confirmed 86-12 on July 13, 2017. He announced in July 2019 that he would resign to run for the Senate.

Won the 2020 Republican primary for the open seat of retiring Sen. Lamar Alexander and defeated Democrat Marquita Bradshaw in the general election, 1,840,926 votes to 1,040,691. He took office January 3, 2021.

Serves on the Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs, Foreign Relations, Appropriations, and Rules and Administration committees. Wikipedia credits him with drafting the GENIUS Act, a stablecoin law signed July 18, 2025.
Was unopposed in the August 6, 2026 Republican primary (623,538 votes). According to his official biography, he and his wife Chrissy live in Davidson County and have four children.

record.text: Serves on the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee, chairing its Subcommittee on National Security and International Trade and Finance.
Serves on the Senate Appropriations Committee, chairing its Subcommittee on Financial Services and General Government.
Serves on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee as ranking member of its Subcommittee on State Department and USAID Management, International Operations, and Bilateral International Development.

candidates.name: Marquita Bradshaw
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 6, 2026 Democratic primary with 54.7% of the vote

summary.text: Marquita Bradshaw is a Memphis-born environmental-justice advocate and community organizer, and the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate. She was the Democratic nominee for this seat in 2020, losing to Bill Hagerty, lost the 2024 Democratic Senate primary to Gloria Johnson, and won the 2026 primary. She is the founder and executive director of Sowing Justice.

background.text: Born January 12, 1974 and raised in Memphis, Tennessee; her parents helped organize residents around contamination at the Memphis Defense Depot Superfund site.
Earned a high school diploma from Central High School and a bachelor's degree from the University of Memphis (a Bachelor of Liberal Studies in journalism and communication studies, per Wikipedia).

Her career and advocacy work, according to her Ballotpedia survey, has spanned labor, environmental, education-reform, tax-reform, trade-policy and social-justice causes; she has worked as a caretaker for a differently abled adult and says she experienced medical bankruptcy.

Wikipedia reports she chairs the environmental justice committee of the Sierra Club's Tennessee chapter, and has worked with the Mid-South Peace and Justice Center, the AFL-CIO, the Sierra Club and Tennesseans for Fair Taxation.

Won the 2020 Democratic Senate primary with 35.5% in a five-candidate field, becoming the first Black woman nominated for statewide office by a major party in Tennessee, per Wikipedia. She lost the general election to Bill Hagerty, about 62% to 35%.
Founded Sowing Justice after the 2020 race, which she describes as a nonpartisan organization focused on civic engagement beyond voting; she serves as its executive director.
Lost the 2024 Democratic Senate primary to Gloria Johnson, then won the August 6, 2026 Democratic primary with 54.7% of the vote over four opponents.

priorities.text: Build an economy that works for working people, including ensuring a living wage and restructuring the tax system to shift the burden of income, sales, and property taxes away from working Americans.
Pursue a transition away from fossil fuels toward renewable energy, framed as reducing energy costs and pollution-driven healthcare burdens.
Expand comprehensive healthcare coverage, including mental, dental, vision, and reproductive health services, and support rural hospitals.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for a 'just transition to a circular economy' focused on renewable energy and says the campaign will pursue 'bold environmental and climate action.'
positions.quote: Break our dependency on fossil with a just transition to a circular economy which focus on clean renewable energy, affordable housing, public transportation, expanding Medicare, and green jobs.

positions.summary: Supports expanding Medicare to address the health burdens of pollution and climate change, and says healthcare legislation must comprehensively cover mental, dental, vision, and reproductive care.
positions.quote: Expanding Medicare for all to mitigate the disproportionate burdens of pollution and climate change.

positions.summary: Calls for restructuring what she describes as a regressive tax system to remove the tax burden from working Americans.
positions.quote: Restructure the regressive tax system to fairly tax all working Americans, removing the burden of income, sales & property taxes from the working population.

positions.summary: Lists ensuring a living wage as part of her economic platform.
Emphasizes quality childcare and wrap-around services for working families, and supports universal pre-K.
positions.quote: Supports universal pre-K education giving children the foundation to be lifelong learners

summary.text: Andrew Gerena is an independent candidate for U.S. Senate who describes himself as a working-class American with experience in military service, security, commercial trucking, information technology, food service and scientific research.

background.text: Says he has life and employment experience ranging from military service to security, commercial trucking, information technology, food service and scientific research.
Earned an associate degree from Bryant & Stratton College in 2014; Ballotpedia lists his career experience as a technician.
Describes himself as a hiker, runner, motorcyclist and do-it-yourselfer, and says he is running with no political connections or financial support.

priorities.text: Lists a series of specific policy positions including repealing Tennessee restrictions on rent price controls, right-to-repair protections for farmers, pro-nuclear energy, repealing the Patriot Act, and ending U.S. involvement in what he calls regime-change wars.

positions.summary: Calls for repealing Tennessee's state-level restrictions on local rent price controls.
positions.quote: Repealing Tennessee's Restrictions against enacting ANY reasonable rent price controls.

summary.text: Robert Jones is an independent candidate for U.S. Senate who describes himself as a historian, educator, business owner, archaeologist and nonprofit leader. He says he accepts no campaign donations and has no political party directing his decisions.

background.text: Describes himself as a historian, educator, business owner, archaeologist, nonprofit leader, husband and father.
Says he holds a Ph.D. in Classics, a master's degree in Military History, an M.B.A., a bachelor's degree in Corporate Finance and a certificate in Strategic Management.

Says he teaches history, has taken part in archaeological research in the United States and abroad, founded his first business at 17, has helped build and operate veterinary practices with his wife, and directs a farm-animal sanctuary.
Says he accepts no campaign donations and has no political party directing his decisions.

priorities.text: Created and signed a 'Public Service Pledge' committing to principles including equal representation, evidence before opinion, transparency, fiscal responsibility, civil discourse, and accountability, along with a proposed 'Accountability Framework' for constituent oversight of his Senate office.

summary.text: James Macon III is an independent candidate for U.S. Senate who describes himself as a global business strategist with more than 25 years of Fortune 500 leadership experience, a former journalist and a former pastor. He says he is running on lower costs, better jobs and stronger communities.

background.text: Ballotpedia lists a high school diploma from East St. Louis Senior High School and graduate degrees from Northern Illinois University (2002) and the University of Tennessee (2005); he says these are an MA and an MBA, respectively.
Served in the U.S. Air National Guard in 2010, according to Ballotpedia.
Says he is a Senior Director at Stryker with prior executive roles at Medtronic and Wright Medical, and more than 25 years of Fortune 500 leadership experience.
Says his background includes five years as a journalist, including for CNN, and a decade of church leadership as a pastor, administrative pastor and educator.
Says he has been married to his wife, Monica, for 16 years and is a father.

priorities.text: Focuses on lowering costs, creating jobs, and building stronger communities, including advanced manufacturing, infrastructure investment, and workforce training.

summary.text: David Sutman Jr. is an independent candidate for U.S. Senate who describes himself as a working-class Tennessean and political outsider, and Ballotpedia lists his career experience as a truck driver. He says he is running to focus on cost-of-living issues and government accountability.

background.text: Ballotpedia lists his career experience as working as a truck driver.
Describes himself as a working-class Tennessean and political outsider who was raised with values of hard work, personal responsibility and community.
Says he has spent his career 'solving real-world problems' and creating opportunities rather than navigating political circles.

priorities.text: Says the federal government should refocus on policies that ease the cost burden on working families, including support for small businesses and economic growth.
Emphasizes government transparency and accountability to constituents over party loyalty.

summary.text: Tharon Chandler is an independent candidate for U.S. Senate who ran as an independent in the 2024 Senate race in Tennessee. He was born in Lawrenceburg, Tennessee, and Ballotpedia lists his career experience as including work as a journalist, economist, Christian missionary and conservationist.

background.text: Born William Tharon Chandler in Lawrenceburg, Tennessee; graduated from Lawrence County High School.

Served in the U.S. Army in 1991 and earned a bachelor's degree from Memphis State University in 1994. He also completed graduate-level coursework and studied education at the University of Tennessee at Martin, the University of North Alabama and Middle Tennessee State University.

Ballotpedia lists his career experience as including work as a journalist, economist, Christian missionary and conservationist, and affiliations with Gulf War Veterans Against the War, Wounded Warriors, the Fraternal Order of Police and the YMCA.
Ran as an independent in the 2024 U.S. Senate election in Tennessee, receiving 0.9% (28,444 votes) in the general election won by Marsha Blackburn.

summary.text: Jeremy Hearn is an independent candidate on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot for U.S. Senate. No campaign website or public policy statements were found.
Yoshi Matthews is an independent candidate on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot for U.S. Senate. No campaign website or public policy statements were found.

Catherine 'Barcy' Whitson is an independent candidate for U.S. Senate. According to her campaign website, she had a career in the insurance industry and has spent about 20 years as a volunteer life coach, pastor and mentor.

background.text: According to her campaign website, she had a successful career in the insurance industry before spending the last 20 years volunteering as a life coach, pastor and mentor.
Says she is running for the 2027-2033 term to promote 'What Tennesseans Want' and is on the ballot as an independent, and goes by Barcy.

researchNotes: Bill Hagerty did not complete Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey and no accessible press-release archive was found on his official Senate site during this research pass, so his stated 2026 campaign positions are not documented here beyond his committee roles; his federal key votes and FEC totals are added separately by script. Tharon Chandler, Jeremy Hearn, Yoshi Matthews, and Catherine Whitson are independent candidates with no Candidate Connection survey responses or discoverable campaign websites/public statements as of this research pass. Biography pass: Jeremy Hearn and Yoshi Matthews have no campaign website, Ballotpedia survey or biography available, so their entries remain ballot-status only; Andrew Mixon (Federalist Party) is listed by Ballotpedia as withdrawn or disqualified and is not profiled. The existing Hagerty text calling Mitt Romney 'Governor' was corrected, since the sources say only 'Mitt Romney'.
